explicit_validation.explanation: The paper explicitly validates LLM judge against human evaluation by performing Spearman correlation analysis between LLM judge criteria and human edit operation annotations using the German4All-Annotated dataset

prompts.notes: Prompt is written in German, includes one-shot example, uses structured JSON outputs; full prompt description is in subsection F.2 of the appendix

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Considering the low number of annotators, the content-related questions show a decent average agreement

guidelines.notes: Evaluation questions provided: Q1 (content preservation), Q2 (information addition), Q3 (information loss), Q4 (type of addition), Q5 (complexity rating); originally conducted in German

sample_size.validated_by_both: German4All-Annotated subset (exact size not specified, but contains corrected test set of 150 samples)
sample_size.notes: Validation performed on manually corrected German4All-Annotated subset

quantitative_scores.notes: Correlation between 'corrected info' human operation and LLM content preservation
Correlation between 'removed info' human operation and LLM information addition
Correlation between 'hallucination in origin' human operation and LLM information addition
Correlation between 'added info' human operation and LLM information loss
Correlation between 'adjusted complexity' human operation and LLM complexity level

validation_results.summary_finding: Gemma-3-27B-it shows statistically significant correlations with human annotations for content preservation, information addition, and complexity level, but struggles with detecting missing information.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM judge evaluates similar criteria as humans but with slightly different framing; human evaluation includes additional operational annotations
